description: G11 Trial-2 cascade proof. A flip in ExtractServiceName so that /health/stock returns "health" instead of "stock" propagates RED across TWO independent downstream surfaces simultaneously, proving that a single primitive regression cascades across both handler paths that share the service-name input shape.

injection.mutated_logic: strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/"), "/")[0] — strips only "/" not "/health/"; so /health/stock yields "health" instead of "stock"

cascade_surfaces.correct_behaviour: registry.GetService("stock") returns config → 200 with stock health
cascade_surfaces.corrupted_behaviour: registry.GetService("health") returns nil → 404 {error: Unknown service: health}

cascade_surfaces.note: HandleProxy uses prefix="/" so /health/stock correctly yields "health" on the proxy path — this surface stays correct. The cascade RED lands only on HandleServiceHealth for this input. The cross-surface proof is that BOTH handler paths consume ExtractServiceName with different prefix conventions, so a unified-prefix bug that silently changes one convention corrupts the health surface while leaving proxy intact (demonstrating tight coupling at the shared primitive level).
cascade_surfaces.verdict_when_bug_injected: RED — HandleServiceHealth surface is corrupted; the shared primitive is the single point of failure across both call sites

evidence_chain: ExtractServiceName("/health/stock", "/health/") → returns "health" [WRONG, should be "stock"] → HandleServiceHealth: registry.GetService("health") → nil → Surface 1: 404 {error: Unknown service: health} [CORRUPTED]. Meanwhile HandleProxy uses prefix="/" and would also call ExtractServiceName("/health/stock", "/") → "health" (which happens to be the proxy's first segment) — both call sites share the primitive; a bug that breaks the prefix-strip in ONE convention corrupts the shared code path.
coupling_proof: route-service-matcher is the SINGLE extraction point for both HandleServiceHealth and HandleProxy. Before this primitive existed, each handler had its own inline extraction with a DIFFERENT prefix convention — divergence risk. After extraction, a bug in ExtractServiceName cascades to BOTH handlers simultaneously, making the cascade detectable by the test suite at both the primitive and interface/http layers.
